_comment: Mentors listed on mentors.html — the final 2026 cohort. Descriptions are condensed from each mentor's own words in the BSRI Mentor Application Form (Responses); that form's stated purpose is mentor information for the website. Portraits are matched by filename in assets/img/mentors/; the Drive sources live in data/headshot-sources.local.json, which is gitignored because a Drive file id is a capability, not just a label.

mentors.name: Prasun Datta
mentors.affil: PhD student · Rensselaer Polytechnic Institute
mentors.blurb: Works on the mathematical foundations of deep learning — how networks learn representations through gradient-based optimisation, why some learned features generalise, and how adversarial training reshapes hidden layers. The aim is rigorous theory for why deep networks work, when they fail, and how to make them reliable.

mentors.name: Imranur Rahman
mentors.affil: PhD student · North Carolina State University
mentors.blurb: Studies software security, particularly the attack surface created by vulnerable dependencies in the software supply chain. His work measures the costs and benefits of different dependency declaration methods as a way of reducing exposure to n-day attacks.

mentors.name: Sk Ruhul Azgor
mentors.affil: PhD student · Pennsylvania State University
mentors.blurb: Works in theoretical computer science, on approximation algorithms, graph theory, linear graph layouts and dynamic algorithms.

mentors.name: Rasman Mubtasim Swargo
mentors.affil: Master’s student · Missouri University of Science and Technology
mentors.blurb: Applies machine learning to systems, focusing on high-performance data transfer across wide-area research networks. He designs adaptive controllers that replace brittle hand-tuned heuristics with reinforcement learning, tested on research testbeds such as FABRIC and CloudLab.

mentors.name: Md Kamruzzaman Kamrul
mentors.affil: PhD student · Purdue University
mentors.blurb: Applies machine learning and natural language processing across finance and civil engineering, including large language models for time-series forecasting and deepfake detection, alongside work on the seismic response of soil and embankments.

mentors.name: Ferdous Bin Ali
mentors.affil: Industry researcher · VISIE Ltd.
mentors.blurb: Builds multi-agent architectures for domains including fintech and bioinformatics, and is exploring quantum machine learning algorithms.

mentors.name: Abdul Muntakim Rafi
mentors.affil: PhD student · University of British Columbia
mentors.blurb: Works on machine learning for regulatory genomics — predicting how DNA sequence determines gene expression, and what that reveals about the non-coding genome.

mentors.name: Tasnim Islam
mentors.affil: PhD student · University of Maryland, Baltimore County
mentors.blurb: Develops machine learning for biomedical signals on wearable devices, including real-time stress detection from ECG and PPG data as a scalable alternative to clinic-based mental health assessment.

mentors.name: Sultan Ahmed
mentors.affil: PhD student · University of Maryland, Baltimore County
mentors.blurb: Works across machine learning, cybersecurity and agentic AI, with applications in healthcare.

mentors.name: Pranta Saha
mentors.affil: PhD student · University of California, Davis
mentors.blurb: Integrates solid-state defects — excellent spin qubits — with high-index nanophotonic devices, building hardware for on-chip quantum information processing.

mentors.name: Moonzarin Reza
mentors.affil: PhD student · Texas A&M University
mentors.blurb: Works at the intersection of machine learning and cosmology, using simulation-based inference to recover cosmological parameters from Type Ia supernova light curves.

mentors.name: Syeda Lammim Ahad
mentors.affil: Postdoctoral fellow · Waterloo Centre for Astrophysics
mentors.blurb: Studies how galaxies form and evolve across cosmic time in different environments, using cosmological hydrodynamic simulations and photometric surveys to analyse large samples of galaxies and clusters — and to ask when, how and why galaxies stop forming stars.

mentors.name: Tabassum S Tanvir
mentors.affil: Postdoctoral researcher · Iowa State University
mentors.blurb: Studies star and planet formation: how turbulence and initial mass function variations shape stellar birth, and how non-ideal magnetohydrodynamic effects govern protoplanetary disc evolution and the growth of planetary embryos.

mentors.name: Shahriar Muhammad Nahid
mentors.affil: Postdoctoral researcher · Stanford University
mentors.blurb: Probes the physics of low-dimensional materials to build multifunctional opto-electro-mechanical nanodevices, with the goal of unconventional memory, logic and energy-harvesting devices that cut the energy cost of computation.

mentors.name: Md Shafayet Ullah Bhuiyan
mentors.affil: PhD student · Stevens Institute of Technology
mentors.blurb: Fabricates and characterises nanomaterials experimentally, and models them computationally — molecular dynamics, finite element analysis, and machine learning applied to mechanical engineering problems.

mentors.name: Rafsan Al Shafatil Islam Subad
mentors.affil: PhD student · University of Maryland, College Park
mentors.blurb: Develops functional nanomaterials and scalable manufacturing for printed and flexible electronics, including metal-free 3D-printable inks from functionalised carbon nanomaterials for RF devices, antennas and sensors. Previously built soft tactile sensors for underwater robotics.

mentors.name: Md Minaruzzaman
mentors.affil: PhD student · The Ohio State University
mentors.blurb: Studies how nuclear materials behave under irradiation, combining theoretical and computational modelling with hands-on experiment so that simulations can be validated against real observations.

mentors.name: Md Maruf Tahmid
mentors.affil: Faculty member · Bangladesh Army University of Engineering & Technology
mentors.blurb: Works on computational fluid dynamics and heat transfer, including conjugate mixed convection and solar air heaters, alongside density functional theory and bio-inspired aerofoil aerodynamics.

mentors.name: Arafat Anzir
mentors.affil: PhD student · Texas State University
mentors.blurb: Works where bio-inspired materials meet computational mechanics and deep learning. He analyses CT scan data of pangolin scales to understand how natural armour achieves damage tolerance, and applies physics-informed neural networks to biomechanical prediction.

mentors.name: Nusrat Subah Binte Shakhawat
mentors.affil: PhD student · Federation University Australia
mentors.blurb: Builds an integrated framework for power system reliability under rising renewable penetration, and for resilience against increasingly frequent natural disasters — aimed at flexible distribution systems and microgrids built around distributed energy resources.

mentors.name: Rahul Sarker
mentors.affil: University of Calgary
mentors.blurb: Uses low-value biomass — specifically aspen fibre — in fused filament fabrication to make wood-PLA biocomposites, working on the chemical treatments that let hydrophilic wood fibre bond with a hydrophobic polymer matrix, and on how much fibre a print can carry before it clogs.

mentors.name: Feroz Islam
mentors.affil: Postdoctoral researcher · Wageningen University & Research
mentors.blurb: Works on flood risk and water resources management, climate-smart agriculture and food security, using hydrological models, IoT sensing and data-driven tools to study climate stresses and how to adapt to them.

mentors.name: M. Kifayath Chowdhury
mentors.affil: PhD student · Delft University of Technology
mentors.blurb: Studies how climate change reshapes river systems, using data analysis and hydro-morphological modelling. The insights help river managers plan interventions for flood control, freshwater supply and navigation.

mentors.name: Fajle Rabbi Ashik
mentors.affil: PhD student · McGill University
mentors.blurb: Studies how built-environment interventions change travel behaviour and well-being.
